A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is possible to do word segmentation without a lexicon, and with only minimal training data.

we are able to obtain good performance with only unsegmented training texts, which is a very important result for the Japanese language, where there is no standard word segmentation algorithm, and no large annotated corpus available.

our method is able to learn a statistical model of Japanese word boundaries from unsegmented data and to use this model in a variety of applications, including segmentation, part-of-speech tagging, and named entity recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
statistical segmentation can be performed with very little supervision, and can be applied to kanji as well as kana.
the statistical method can be competitive with the best morphological analyzers, even when the training data is not annotated for segmentation and the test data is not annotated at all.
the task of Japanese segmentation can be approached from a purely statistical perspective without the need to resort to a morphological analysis.
